ai.seo_question: Who is Manat in the context of pre-Islamic Arabian polytheism?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase specifically identifies Manat as the third deity in the Quraysh's triad, often discussed alongside Al-Lat and Al-Uzza to illustrate the pre-Islamic Arab conception of divine intercession. The mention underscores the Quranic critique of attributing daughterhood to Allah, a key theological point refuted in the subsequent verses to establish pure monotheism.
